title: Feedback please
author: hannemaster
selftext:
Sorry for recording with phone!

Codex helped me a lot with the code. 

I wanted to make a single room and try to implement everything I want in the game. Not quite there yet.

Hero and enemy are placeholders from mixamo, will replace eventually. I’m particularly proud of the breaking pots. Any and all feedback is welcome.  Any ideas on making it better?

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
it looks decently put together. I dont understand why the action bar is so colorful but that is a minor nitpick.

You are already using Codex. You can be a bit more ambitious and make more content/mechanics etc.

replies.author: hannemaster
replies.body: Thanks! Yea colorful action bar I created before deciding to go this style. Still need to adjust it. Yes I’m planning to add much more. Also to increase the world to make it more feel alive. Like adding spiders or stuff like that crawling on the floor.

comments.author: Mahazael
comments.body:
Can I ask you what game engine are you using? I'm struggling a lot to make a good UI with Codex + Unity game 😞  
Yours looks pretty cool!

replies.author: hannemaster
replies.body: Yes, I’m using latest Godot. I feel that it is a lot easier to use than Unity. Very lightweight and easier to understand. Also very small to download(like 150mb instead of gigabytes). I have not found any downsides or missing features. I was also pretty surprised about the power of shader effects in Godot.

replies.author: Mahazael
replies.body: Just curious about one thing if you wanna share: It's the game 100% AI generated (with your 'engineered' prompts) or you are still doing some manual things in the editor / code?

replies.author: hannemaster
replies.body: Depends. Simple systems I write myself and let codex optimize it. Complex systems I ask codex to write and tell it to put all variables in inspector so I can finetune them.

replies.author: UsualObvious4668

replies.author: Paran01d7Andr01d
replies.body: Try Meshy?

replies.body: Thanks! I'll give it a try. I've pivoted to 2d for the moment to get the game worked out and playa me, then I plan on converting it to 3D, already got those in the plans lol

comments.author: rmfrost
comments.body:
From a game design perspective, what benefit is there in requiring players to manually run over every individual coin that falls to the ground? Immersion? Nostalgia? Tension for looting things while in combat?

Would it be harmful to the intended player experience to just have stuff auto-looted? Or, at least, gold auto-looted?

replies.author: hannemaster
replies.body: Yes you’re right. I do have an auto pickup but I still need to increase the range.

replies.author: United-Bell-382
replies.body:
Instead of increasing range you can find a keybind like Z to trigger the player to pick up stuff automatically from the ground that way you can always pick up items not worrying about losing something.

Adding a small label to item on the ground and having the option to show or hide it could also help detect item from the ground.

These are all ideas from a very old game called Dungeon Siege btw but I think they fit here perfectly. 

Looks good so far, looking forward for more

replies.author: hannemaster
replies.body: Thanks mate! Good idea!

comments.body: looks cool man. im doing something similar but in 2D for diablo 1/2, BG influence. good luck to you

replies.author: hannemaster
replies.body: Thanks mate! Started in 2d isometric but the sprites I needed to generate were so much. The hero animation alone were like 4 animations \* 60 frames \* 8 directions. And then I ran into the issue of wanting more than one weapon. So 3d made that kind of stuff way easier.

replies.author: j05h187
replies.body:
Yep haha ive been thru abit of pain but gotten my techniques down a little for generating enemies/directionals on a budget.

3D intimidated me abit with rendering clothes/armours, would be kinda nasty having to render all the different items on the character model that you eventually want to have in an RPG, or how'd you find that?

With 2D im thinking to just generate a new character 'skin' every 10-20 levels, reflecting your battle prowess and levelling up. kinda like an mtx skin but 2D

replies.author: hannemaster
replies.body: I haven’t looked into clothing just yet but I believe swapping weapons is quite easy because it is a separate object which should just follow the hand bone.

comments.author: OverratedHyperbole
comments.body: Nice job man. One major UI change: you need to differentiate damage numbers from the enemy vs. the numbers you are dealing to enemies. It can be size, color, animation, etc something that let's me know which damage ticker I'm doing and what the enemy is doing. I think everything else will come later like improvements of visual design and UI. But this one is a major design necessity.

comments.author: pigeonocchio
comments.body:
Looks great. Something I realised quickly is that animations are a pain. Mixamo gets you going but as soon as you want something better you need to find the animation. Say you want to have your character do a sword dash or something, sure...where's the animation. Then you'll go down the rabbit hole of video to animation perhaps, i.e. cheap mocap. 

Mixamo have a good wizard collection, maybe you could go for a ranged spell caster next with some projectile and particle effects, aoe damage, spell sounds?
